modules.reason: createWatcherFaultProofProgressAuthority is one state owner: admission, execution updates, reconciliation and completion close over one objective index, decision cache and authority epoch, and share their revision checks; splitting it would redesign that ownership rather than separate independent declarations. W1 (+15): the authority pins each open objective's L1 history in the follower and releases it once the objective's completion marker holds (E1 ruling). F-fix (+1): completion markers are made and matched at the follower's k (the deployment's security parameter), read once from the retention. F-fix (+17): a pin that pruning beat is remembered per objective and retried on each later new observation, so the objective stays open and named rather than silently unheld. W2b-fix (+10): the authority opens its decision journal and initializes through the journals' shared opener, so a journal that could not be opened, or one that failed integrity, is retried by the next use instead of being cached. W2b-fix R2 (+91): an objective whose workflow names a decision the journal does not hold is held by name (journal_decision_missing) at startup, admission and execution update instead of failing the process, takes no new work while held, and clears once its header leaves the finalized queue; the holds share the objective index, retention pins and table rows this owner keeps. W3 (+16): the authority answers whether an execution's completion is already marked beyond rollback recovery, so the supervisor neither holds that released history again nor verifies it again. DLH (+14): an objective that stops being driven (held under any name, completed, or its header left the finalized queue with no signed attempt to reconcile) is reported to the execution, which drops its refusal hold (fault_proof_l1_refused) that no later run or completion check would clear. WBF (-49): the native-progress wake-up had no producer and is gone; the decision driver's per-pass queue observation is the wake-up. DLH2 (+8): an unheld objective with no signed attempt whose header left the finalized queue is released by the same rule as a resolved hold (pin, in-memory entry and unfinished count at once; its rows unless a job of it is still queued or active), instead of staying open and pinned forever and being adopted again on every restart. DLH3 (+35): a released objective, and a completion marked beyond rollback recovery once its header leaves the queue, are forgotten in process through the objective cleanup owner (fault-proof-objective-cleanup.ts), which removes the workflow directory with its rows, instead of leaving directories forever and marked rows until the next start; a queue row a crash left queued or active no longer pins the objective, and the authority names directories it could not remove.
